records.question: Which Supreme Court money-case dates are coming up?
records.answer: 7 dates are set across the 5 live Supreme Court money cases; the next is October 23, 2026 (DHS v. D.V.D.: Government merits brief due). 5 of them are not on the library's waiting list yet. Custodia's October 28, 2026 date is the library's scheduling inference, not a court date.

records.question: What has actually happened after an executive order was signed?
records.answer: Only 4 of the 509 orders on the record have any follow-through written up in the library's confirmed list of changes: 7 records on EO 14178, EO 14215, EO 14395, EO 14431. 3 deadlines set by EO 14395 have passed with no public record of the deliverables. For the other orders the library has no dated record of what happened next, which is not the same as nothing happening.

records.question: Which Trump executive orders are still in force, and which were revoked, replaced or expired?
records.answer: Of the 509 Trump executive orders on the library's record, 439 have no revocation on record in the library's reading (282 of the 288 second-term orders). 51 were revoked, 8 replaced by a later order, 2 partly replaced and 1 terminated; 5 had their operative date pass and 3 still wait for a Federal Register number. 72 rows carry a check flag.

records.question: Which parts of the national fraud-detection system are proven, and which are only announced or missing?
records.answer: Of the 33 parts of the national fraud-detection system the library mapped, 18 are proved by a public record, 7 are announced with no public text, 2 are proposed and 2 are the library's inference. 4 are missing: Technical annex / SLA, NFDC system records, Collected recovery and Correction, notice and remedy path. Since the map, Treasury reported pre-payment verification fully operating on September 30, 2026.

records.question: How does a federal grant actually travel from Congress to a city, and what records prove each step?
records.answer: Congress sets the purpose and budget authority, OMB apportions it, HUD makes the prime awards (for FY2024 HOME: $23,907,179 to New York's Housing Trust Fund Corporation and $1,303,112.35 directly to the City of Syracuse), Treasury's Fiscal Service pays, and auditors test afterward. Of the 13 links in the route, 5 rest on a published award, outlay or audit record; 2 (the payments on to Home HeadQuarters) are still open, with no dated payment on the public record.

records.question: How does money move between Treasury, the Fed, the GSEs, the trust funds and the IMF?
records.answer: The federal tree records 16 money relationships among 20 bodies. 10 of them run through the Treasury: 8 point into it (revenue in, customs receipts / approved refunds, profits remitted, holds the public debt, intragovernmental IOUs, conservatorship dividends) and 2 point out (quota / dues (up & out), backstop / guarantee). The other 6 are seized assets, internal lending, quota / dues (up & out), ownership capital & dividends, state equity stakes. None of the 16 is dated in the master.

records.question: What changed in U.S. federal institutions and records, month by month, from January 2025 to September 2026?
records.answer: The library's dated record holds 60 changes in federal institutions and records from January 20, 2025 to August 28, 2026. The busiest months were January 2025 (7), February 2025 (7), August 2026 (6). By the hub's seven clocks, the ones that moved most often were record (23), rules (20), authority (19). The newest, on August 28, 2026: “Ninth Circuit hears the appeal in AFGE v. OPM; four OPM RIF, probation and suitability appeal rules take effect September 2.” None of these rows has its official link attached yet, so each one is marked as needing a primary source.

records.question: What changed in money rules, international institutions and standards, month by month, from January 2025 to September 2026?
records.answer: The library's dated record holds 59 changes in money rules, international institutions and standards from January 30, 2025 to September 1, 2026. The busiest months were June 2026 (10), March 2026 (8), May 2026 (7). By the hub's seven clocks, the ones that moved most often were rules (39), authority (18), reliance (15). The newest, on September 1, 2026: “SEC issues a transfer-agent-modernization proposal that permits DLT-linked master-file architectures while retaining one accountable recordkeeping …” None of these rows has its official link attached yet, so each one is marked as needing a primary source.

records.question: What has actually changed in the federal government, and how far has each change gone?
records.answer: 31 confirmed changes are on record. 26 have reached a named stage on the ladder (from authority created to operating), and 5 are still waiting on a specific record before they count; 2 of the staged changes also have their next record named and pending. Each card keeps the before and after, who was involved, and what the record does not prove.

records.question: Which federal changes has the research found but not yet written up as recorded changes?
records.answer: 18 federal changes, dated September 17, 2026 to September 22, 2026, have been researched with a before and after and an official source but are not yet written up in the movement registry. Among them: FY2026 standardized rating and performance-award controls (Office of Personnel Management); Polysilicon anti-stockpiling import gate (Bureau of Industry and Security); Fort Carson and Pinon Canyon withdrawal extension PLO 7971 (Bureau of Land Management); Temporary moratorium on certain ACA Marketplace agent and broker registration (Department of Health and Human Services and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services). The research accepted all 18; each card prints its review decision and what the record does not prove.

records.question: Which federal bodies are on the government's own books, and which sit outside?
records.answer: Of the 352 bodies on the federal tree (committees counted separately), 271 are counted in the government's own audited statements. 26 are disclosed but kept off the books (Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac, Amtrak, The Federal Reserve System), 13 are related parties the U.S. influences but does not control (Federal Home Loan Banks, IMF, IBRD), and 33 sit outside (Farm Credit System, Brand USA, In-Q-Tel); 9 have no placement yet. The test is the federal accounting standard SFFAS 47. The 25 Reserve Bank branch offices are listed too and counted with their Reserve Bank; Buffalo is closed but stays listed.
